camera_qos.rationale: Matches the real drivers (tk26_vision config/realsense_qos.yaml). Every tk26_vision CameraInfo subscription and several image subscriptions are RELIABLE; a best-effort publisher delivers zero messages to them, silently.

raycast.rationale: 57 x 349 = 19893 rays at 10 Hz = 198930 points/s, against the Mid-360's 200000, with ~1.03 deg spacing in both axes over its -7..+52 deg by 360 deg field. sweep spreads ray firing across the frame via ray_time_offsets, which the plugin treats as a firing SCHEDULE (the USD schema documents only the pose extrapolation, not the deferral): without it the whole pattern is cast every physics step, measured 27.89 vs 4.47 ms/step in an empty room. VOID COST NUMBERS REMOVED 2026-09-11: this field used to quote +0.75 s of compute per simulated second at full scale, +0.50 at 32x360, +0.25 at 16x360 and +0.22 at 8x360, described as nearly flat below 16x360. Every one of those was measured BEFORE the scene-query fix, i.e. with PhysX building no scene query manager and EVERY RAY MISSING, so they timed rays that never resolved a hit or touched a collision shape; they understate the true cost by roughly 7x. Measured after the fix, live in navigation-parity on arena rcw2026 (RTF, higher is better): at 120 Hz physics the occupancy lidar runs 0.248 and this full 57x349 fan 0.151, so the sensor's marginal cost is ~2.6 s of compute per simulated second at that rate. Cost scales with the PHYSICS rate because each ray is a scene query paid per physics step: at 40 Hz physics / 40 Hz control the same full fan runs 0.514 and the 44x349 shipped DEFAULT runs 0.578. Note the 120 Hz occupancy figure: the simulator is already under RTF 0.5 at the validated default rate with NO raycast sensor at all, so ray count is not what puts a default run under that floor -- the rate is. Treat any raycast sizing figure dated before 2026-09-09 as void for the same reason. min_range_m matches the hardware pointcloud_to_laserscan range_min and offsets each ray's START; raising it does NOT recover cost (0.2 -> 0.7 m moved cost 3%) because the expense is testing rays against the robot's shapes, not hitting them. max_range_m is the datasheet range and is nearly free (8 m vs 40 m differed under 4%). self_filter drops returns on the robot's own body: 9840 of 19893 points (49.5%) hit the robot, an artefact of the over-approximated convex-hull COLLISION geometry the raycast sees rather than the visual shape a real Mid-360 would; identifying them needs report_hit_prim_paths, which was ORIGINALLY measured at 31.95 vs 31.91 ms/step and called free -- that measurement is VOID, taken while PhysX scene queries were disabled so no ray hit anything and no path was ever resolved. Re-measured live with rays actually hitting, at 40 Hz physics / 40 Hz control in the arena: self_filter on RTF 0.514, off 0.590 -- about 0.25 s of compute per simulated second. Turning it off is NOT a usable option (the frame then carries ~9840 self-hits and walls the robot in), but a cheaper self-filter is the largest single RTF lever left in this sensor.
